cards.name: Drifting fog / smoke haze
cards.summary: A slow grey fractal fog drifts across the shot at low opacity while the grade lifts the blacks, so the scene reads as smoky or misty.
use_for: war, riot or fire aftermath shots in a documentary
dawn or monsoon atmosphere over a skyline
background plate under a chapter card
avoid: faces in close-up: the fog sits on top of them and greys the skin
fog opacity above ~45: the picture turns into a flat grey wash
news footage that must read as unaltered evidence
cards.keyframes_note: Static look; the drift is the Evolution ramp (240 deg per 10 s) plus a slow pan (Premiere 'Pan (Y axis)' 25 deg, After Effects 'Offset Turbulence' 300 px over 10 s). Extend both ramps proportionally for longer clips. Fade it in by keyframing Opacity 0 -> 32 over the first 1 s if the fog must arrive. Premiere's VR noise wraps seamlessly left-right, which is harmless on flat footage. AE points are comp pixels for 1920x1080; scale x and y for other frame sizes (x*W/1920, y*H/1080).

verified.note: Grey fractal fog drifts over the whole shot with lifted blacks; it reads as smoky and the people stay legible.

ae.note: A grey fractal haze drifts over the whole frame with lifted blacks and colour muted to about half its saturation, reading clearly as smoke or mist while the scene stays legible; vs Premiere: close match to Premiere's fog; the AE haze is slightly more even and less patchy.

cards.name: Heat haze shimmer
cards.summary: Low-amplitude turbulent displacement makes the whole frame ripple like air over hot tarmac, with a slight warm push.
avoid: Amount above ~35: it stops reading as heat and becomes a liquid warp
text or graphics on the same clip (they ripple too: put titles on their own track)
talking heads: wobbling faces look like a glitch
cards.keyframes_note: Keep Evolution moving fast (about 270 deg per second) so the shimmer boils; extend the ramp for long clips. Leave Pinning at its default (Pin All) so the frame edges do not pull in. For haze only near the ground, use it on a duplicate of the clip cropped to the lower third on the track above.

verified.note: Wall mouldings, stripe edges and a small round motif carry a fine wavy displacement plus a warm push, readable at full size as heat shimmer.

ae.note: The wall mouldings and stripe edges carry a fine wavy displacement under a warm, slightly more saturated push, readable at full size as heat shimmer; vs Premiere: same strength and warmth as Premiere.

cards.name: Rising embers
cards.summary: Small glowing orange-yellow sparks drift upward from the bottom of frame and fade out, with a soft glow on them.
use_for: burning building, riot or war footage
anger or 'fire' beats in a political explainer
avoid: Premiere: it has no particle generator, so this look is After Effects only (use 'Firelight glow flicker' in Premiere)
dense Birth Rate: it turns into a snowstorm of orange dots
calm or factual news segments
cards.keyframes_note: The simulation runs from the layer's start, so pre-roll: start the layer about 1 s before it is seen (or keyframe Birth Rate [[0, 8], [0.5, 1.5]] for an initial burst) and QC frames at least 1 s in. Negative Gravity makes them rise; Particle Type 5 = Faded Sphere. Glow also blooms the footage's own highlights above threshold 170; raise it if the shot is bright. Cleaner variant: put both effects on a black solid in Add/Screen mode with Composite With Original 0.

verified.note: Only a few tiny orange specks rise in the lower half while the Glow at threshold 170 blooms the bright wall, foreground blocks and flowers into saturated orange-yellow, so the frame reads as an over-glowed grade rather than embers.

previous.why: after_effects changed: On this footage about a quarter of the pixels have a red channel above 170, so the Glow tints the whole wall; at 240 only the lamps, the hottest flowers and the embers themselves (red channel 255) still glow.; not rendered again

cards.name: Firelight glow flicker
cards.summary: A warm orange grade with an amber spotlight pool whose intensity flickers irregularly and amber-bloomed highlights, giving a torch- or fire-lit feel; in the Premiere render the pool landed upper left rather than low in frame, so check where it falls.
use_for: night protest, vigil or torch march
pairs with Rising embers (AE) for fire scenes
dramatic reconstruction of a historic event
avoid: daylight exteriors: a warm flicker with no visible fire source reads as a fault
fast regular flicker: real firelight is irregular, keep the keyframe gaps uneven
Lighting Effects Intensity above ~60: the hotspot blows out
cards.keyframes_note: The flicker keyframes cover 1.5 s; repeat the same uneven pattern (shift by 1.5 s) to the clip length. Premiere flickers the light's Intensity (30-46), After Effects flickers Exposure (-0.1..+0.3 stops). Move the light Center toward where the fire would be (frame fractions in Premiere). Keep Major/Minor Radius under ~40: the gallery render at 60/45 lit most of the frame and blew out the top-left wall instead of reading as a pool low in frame. Render check at Center [0.5, 0.8], radius 38/30, Focus 30: the pool landed upper left (around [0.3, 0.35]) instead of at Center, while a radius-20 spot with Focus 60 (the spotlight pulse recipe) did land on its Center, so check the pool position on a frame before relying on Center with a large, low spot.

verified.note: Re-render: the top-left wall no longer blows out (0.1% near white) and the light flickers unevenly (frame luma swings about 10/255 on the keyed beats), but the whole frame is still graded orange and the round pool landed upper left of the frame instead of low at Center [0.5, 0.8], so it reads as a flickering warm spotlight rather than a fire below; summary rewritten.

ae.note: The whole frame goes strongly orange with the bright wall bloomed amber and the top right close to blown yellow, a torch-lit feel, though the uneven Exposure flicker cannot be judged from two frames; vs Premiere: AE has no light pool, so it warms and blooms the whole frame evenly where Premiere puts a round amber pool upper left.

cards.name: Snowfall
cards.summary: Procedural snow falls over the shot in two depth layers (fine distant flakes plus a few large near flakes) under a cool grade.
use_for: cold, bleak or lonely mood beats
avoid: Premiere: no snow generator, After Effects only
summer or indoor footage
snow added to real news footage presented as real (misleading): keep it on titles, graphics or clearly stylised shots
raising both Flakes and Size far past these values: it becomes a white sheet
cards.keyframes_note: No keyframes needed: CC Snowfall animates on its own and covers the frame from the first frame. The two instances differ in Size, Scene Depth, Speed and Random Seed to give depth. The render check found Size 3-5 / Opacity 50-85 reads as faint 1-2 px specks on a full frame, hence Size 8 and 13 at Opacity 90-95. Composite With Original stays at its default 1 (snow over the image).

verified.note: Dense fine white flakes plus scattered larger flakes cover the whole frame under a cooler, desaturated grade, reading clearly as snow falling in depth.

cards.name: Rainstorm
cards.summary: Fast slanted rain streaks over a darker, cooler, desaturated grade for a stormy monsoon feel.
avoid: Premiere: no rain generator, After Effects only
footage that is visibly sunny or dry
rain added to real news footage presented as real (misleading): keep it to reconstructions, titles or stylised shots
Drops above ~100k: slow renders for no visible gain
cards.keyframes_note: No keyframes needed; drops cover the frame from the first frame. Wind 300 slants the streaks; set Wind negative to slant the other way. Change Random Seed on a second copy for heavier rain. After Effects: at Speed 5000 the Wind 350 streaks rendered almost vertical, so raise Wind (or lower Speed) if the slant must read.

verified.note: Dense thin pale streaks cover the frame over a slightly darker, cooler and much less saturated grade, reading as heavy rain, though the streaks fall almost vertically rather than visibly slanted.

cards.name: Lightning strike flash
cards.summary: A branching white-blue bolt hits the frame while the exposure double-flashes and decays, like a close lightning strike.
use_for: shock reveal or 'thunderbolt' moment in a political explainer
avoid: holding the bolt on screen longer than ~0.4 s: it looks drawn on
factual news footage
flashing more than ~3 times per second (photosensitivity)
cards.keyframes_note: Times are from the strike. Premiere's bolt cannot be faded to nothing (Width minimum 1), so split the clip and put both effects on a 0.35-0.4 s slice that starts at the strike. After Effects fades the bolt with Core/Glow Opacity instead, so it can sit on the whole clip with the keyframes offset to the strike. AE points are comp pixels for 1920x1080; scale x and y for other frame sizes (x*W/1920, y*H/1080).

verified.note: A thin branching blue-white bolt crosses the frame while the exposure flash lifts the whole picture; only a faint residual bolt is left at 1.0 s.

ae.note: At 0.2 s the +1.5-stop flash, applied after the bolt, blows the bolt's blue glow into a broad featureless white beam with no branches readable, and by 1.0 s the frame is clean; vs Premiere: Premiere draws a thin branching blue-white bolt; AE gives a thick blown white streak.

previous.why: after_effects changed: The Exposure keys sit after Lightning and multiply its #7FB8FF glow to clipped white; with Exposure first the double flash still lifts the footage while the white core, forks and blue glow composite on top unclipped.; not rendered again

cards.name: Lens flare sweep
cards.summary: A classic lens flare fades up and travels left to right across the top of frame, like the sun catching the lens.
use_for: skyline, rally or sunrise establishing shots
logo or title reveal (sweep across it)
hope / victory beat in a reel
avoid: no plausible light source in the shot: reads fake
brightness over ~150 on faces or text
neutral news footage (stylised, editorialised)
cards.keyframes_note: 2.5 s sweep; scale the times to the clip. Lens Type is 0-based in Premiere (0 = 50-300mm Zoom) and 1-based in After Effects (1 = the same lens). For a static sun hit, drop the Flare Center keyframes and park it on the real light source. AE points are comp pixels for 1920x1080; scale x and y for other frame sizes (x*W/1920, y*H/1080).

verified.note: A faint small flare at the left at 0.2 s becomes a bright flare with rings at mid-left near the top by 1.0 s, so it fades up and travels left to right.

ae.note: A faint small flare at upper left at 0.2 s becomes a bright flare with ghost rings further right along the top by 1.0 s, so it fades up and travels left to right; vs Premiere: practically identical to Premiere.

cards.name: God rays from above
cards.summary: Warm volumetric light rays stream down from a source above the frame through the bright areas and slowly drift.
avoid: night or very dark footage: the rays are driven by highlights and barely show
faces in the ray path at high Intensity (they wash out)
hard-news footage
cards.keyframes_note: Rays fade up over 0.8 s and the source drifts 16% of the frame width over 6 s; stretch the drift to the clip length and keep it slow. Put the source where a window or sky would be. AE points are comp pixels for 1920x1080; scale x and y for other frame sizes (x*W/1920, y*H/1080).

verified.note: Warm yellow rays stream down through the bright areas; strong (foreground blocks blown, 22% near white) but faces and stripes stay readable.

ae.note: At 1.0 s the rays show only as a small hot warm spot near the top centre with a mild overall lift, with no ray streaks reaching down through the frame; vs Premiere: much weaker than Premiere, which streams strong yellow rays down through the bright areas.

previous.why: after_effects changed: The card's verified demo at Intensity 300 with a 70 px source drew visible radial streaks, while 220 with a 60 px source lights only a spot, so a stronger ramp and a larger emitting area let the rays reach down into the frame.; not rendered again

cards.name: Glint sparkle on highlights
cards.summary: Star-shaped glints twinkle on the brightest highlights (metal, jewellery, water, lights) for a festive or premium sparkle.
use_for: awards, medals, trophies, gold or jewellery shots
avoid: dark frames: glints come from highlights only (lower Highlights Only first)
serious or tragic stories
After Effects version on busy bright frames: every highlight gets a cross streak
cards.keyframes_note: Fade in over 0.4 s; Premiere's Glint shimmers by itself (Shimmer Speed). After Effects has no glint effect: two Glows, one horizontal-only and one vertical-only, draw cross streaks from the hottest highlights; for a twinkle, wobble their Glow Intensity between 0.8 and 1.8 every 0.2-0.4 s.

verified.note: Long star streaks radiate from the small lamps and other highlights with a soft overall sheen.

ae.note: Long horizontal and vertical streaks fire from the small lamps, but the Glow at threshold 210 also washes the upper wall around the left-hand stripes and the flowers in salmon-red, so the frame reads as a red flare grade rather than sparkle on the hottest highlights; vs Premiere: Premiere gives fine white star glints on the lamps with no colour cast.

previous.why: after_effects changed: Here the left-hand white stripe and the bright wall patches have red-channel values between 210 and 240, so at 240 essentially only the lamps (and the hottest flowers) still glow and draw the cross streaks.; not rendered again

cards.name: Soft highlight bloom
cards.summary: Highlights bloom into a soft warm glow and contrast eases off, giving a dreamy, nostalgic or heroic sheen.
use_for: hero shot of a leader or athlete
avoid: Wonder Glow Intensity above ~70 or Size above ~150: the frame turns into a yellow haze (gallery render at 85/120 was overblown)
text-heavy graphics (letters smear)
After Effects Glow Threshold below ~150 (raw 0-255) on daylight footage: the render check blew the frame to white with false-colour blobs
investigative or hard-news segments
cards.keyframes_note: Static look. For a bloom hit on a cut, keyframe Wonder Glow Intensity [[0, 100], [0.4, 70]] (After Effects Glow Intensity [[0, 2.5], [0.4, 0.8]]).

verified.note: Re-render with Wonder Glow 70/40/110: the lamps, the left-hand white stripe and the top-right wall now bloom into a warm cream glow and the whole frame lifts and softens (mean diff about 30/255 against 6 before, 3% near white) while faces and stripes stay readable.

ae.note: The bright wall, lamps and stripe highlights bloom into a warm glow that runs salmon-orange on the wall and near blown at the top right, a strong dreamy sheen; vs Premiere: stronger and more saturated orange than Premiere's cream bloom.

cards.name: Light leak wash over a cut
cards.summary: Film light-leak streaks wash across the cut and keep glowing off the incoming shot before fading. Premiere's Light Leaks effect alone renders cool cyan-blue streaks; the warmth comes from the transition (After Effects carries a warm light-ray bloom instead).
use_for: soft transition between two warm shots
avoid: hard news or serious stories
Light Leaks effect left at full Master for more than ~1 s (it hides the shot)
relying on the effect's colour: its default spectrum renders cool cyan, the warmth comes from the Chroma Leak transition
cards.keyframes_note: Put the transition on the incoming clip (centred on the cut, needs 0.5 s handles both sides) and the effects on the incoming clip's head: times are from that clip's start, so the leak decays over its first 0.9 s. After Effects shows the transition as a cut unless the build gets an ae_preset, so its version carries the whole leak in the effects: a warm-coloured light-ray bloom from the top-left corner plus an exposure lift, both decaying. AE points are comp pixels for 1920x1080; scale x and y for other frame sizes (x*W/1920, y*H/1080).

verified.note: Cool cyan-blue streaks wash over the picture at 0.2 s and are gone by 1.0 s.
verified.recheck: 2026-10-13: re-rendered in live wave 1 (frames the old verdict was judged on: pve/work/gallery_pre_fix/)

previous.why: the verify step rewrote the summary from this render (its rule for 'wrong'); the rewritten card has not been rendered again
re-rendered with the corrected text and values (live wave 1); the new frame matches the corrected card
previous.second_opinion: corrected: rewritten summary said cyan, teal and magenta; measured delta vs the clean 0.2 s frame is about 66% blue, 30% cyan, 3% magenta, so it now says cool cyan-blue

ae.note: At 0.2 s a warm yellow bloom, brightest at the top left, washes most of the frame toward blown (luma about double the clean frame) and by 1.0 s it has fully decayed, a hot leak hit on the cut; vs Premiere: AE washes warm yellow over the whole frame where Premiere lays cool cyan-blue streaks from the right.

cards.name: Film burn cut
cards.summary: The outgoing shot overexposes and warms toward orange-white as a film burn takes it, then the burn clears onto the next shot.
use_for: end of a chapter or era in a documentary
avoid: using it on every cut
short clips without 0.4 s handles on both sides of the cut (centred transition)
text on the incoming shot in the first ~0.4 s (burn residue)
cards.keyframes_note: Effects go on the OUTGOING clip and their times are negative, from its end: the last 0.6-0.7 s overexposes and warms into the cut. The end keys sit at -0.04 (the last frame), never 0: a key time of 0 means the clip START, so [0, peak] plays the move at the head (the gallery render showed exactly that). The 'Burn Chroma' transition goes on the incoming clip, centred on the cut. For a fiery burn-through with glowing holes use the 'Phosphor' transition instead. In After Effects CC Burn Film eats the shot into charred holes that show whatever is below (black on a single track). AE points are comp pixels for 1920x1080; scale x and y for other frame sizes (x*W/1920, y*H/1080).

verified.note: With the end keys at -0.04 the 0.2 s and 1.0 s frames are now clean (identical to the reference) and the burn plays at the tail as intended: from about 1.4 s the shot warms and overexposes until the last frames are blown yellow-orange with dark orange glow blotches (098c, taken at 1.84 s from the same render).

ae.note: Both frames are clean (the 1.0 s frame is identical to the reference) because the burn and exposure keys run only over the last 0.7 s before the cut, which neither sample reaches; vs Premiere: Premiere passed on an extra tail frame at 1.84 s; the AE half needs the same tail sample.

cards.name: Bokeh dream background
cards.summary: The shot racks out of focus into lens bokeh discs and dips slightly darker so text or a cut-out on top stands out.
use_for: background behind a quote card, title or lower-third
night city lights and festival lights
transition into a dream or flashback
avoid: footage without point highlights: it just looks blurry
Gain near 100 on bright skies (blooms to white)
when the background content itself is the evidence
cards.keyframes_note: Rack defocus over 0.8 s, timed so the text lands as the blur peaks. For a static background drop the keyframes (Blur Amount 45 / Blur Radius 30).

verified.note: At 1.0 s the shot is racked fully soft into round bokeh discs and slightly darker; at 0.2 s it is still nearly sharp.

ae.note: At 0.2 s the shot is still nearly sharp and at 1.0 s it is racked fully soft, with highlights spread into soft discs and a slight darkening; vs Premiere: matches Premiere in softness and darkening.

cards.name: Floating dust motes
cards.summary: Sparse soft specks of dust drift slowly through the frame, catching light, for an old-room or sunbeam atmosphere.
use_for: interview B-roll in a sunlit room
pairs with God rays from above
avoid: Premiere: no particle generator, After Effects only
high Birth Rate: it looks like snow
fast-moving or handheld footage (the motes do not track the camera)
cards.keyframes_note: The opening Birth Rate burst seeds the whole volume, then 0.6 keeps it topped up; still QC at >= 1 s of layer time. Velocity and Gravity near zero keep the drift lazy. Pair with God rays from above for dust in a beam.

verified.note: Only scattered cream specks a few pixels wide appear (the 1.0 s frame differs from the clean reference by about 0.5/255 on average), too small and faint to read as dust at normal viewing size.

previous.why: after_effects changed: At Birth Size 0.04 and Max Opacity 55 the motes are a few pixels wide and half transparent; 0.1 is the size at which the ember recipe's sparks read as distinct specks, and higher opacity lets them catch the light.; not rendered again

cards.name: Map location pulse ring
cards.summary: A solid dot marks a place on a map while a thin ring expands from it and fades, repeating like a radar ping.
use_for: marking a city, constituency or incident site on a map
data-viz callout on a chart point
'where it happened' beats in news explainers
avoid: Premiere: no ring generator; use the 'Map / chart region spotlight pulse' recipe or the 'Simple Map Marker' After Effects preset
more than 3-4 simultaneous pings (visual noise)
colours that clash with the map palette
cards.keyframes_note: Three 1.2 s pings; append more pairs to loop. Set both Circle Centers to the location in comp pixels. Edge 3 = Thickness (Contextual Slider = ring thickness px); Blending Mode 2 = Normal keeps the map visible (1 = None would show only the circle). AE points are comp pixels for 1920x1080; scale x and y for other frame sizes (x*W/1920, y*H/1080).

verified.note: The yellow dot and the expanding thin ring read clearly at the frame centre (small ring at 0.2 s, wide faded ring at 1.0 s), but the Glow at threshold 180 also blooms the bright wall and lamps into orange-yellow across the whole picture.

previous.why: after_effects changed: The Glow is meant for the dot and ring (red channel 255) but at 180 it also catches about a fifth of the base picture; at 240 it leaves the map or footage underneath untouched except its hottest whites.; not rendered again

cards.name: Map / chart region spotlight pulse
cards.summary: Everything except one region of a map or chart dims and softens while a warm light pool on the region pulses.
use_for: highlighting a state or district on a map
pointing at one bar, line or number in a chart screenshot
focusing on one face in a group photo
avoid: region near the frame edge (the light pool falls off-frame)
moving footage: the spotlight does not track
Ambience Intensity below ~10: the rest of the map goes black and loses context
cards.keyframes_note: Set the region in both apps: Premiere Center/Position as frame fractions, After Effects Center in comp pixels ([0.62, 0.4] = [1190, 432] in 1920x1080). Premiere pulses the light Intensity 30-50 every 0.8 s; After Effects dims the outside of a feathered circle to 60% black (inverted Circle) and pings a yellow ring twice. Repeat the pulse pairs for longer holds.

verified.note: A warm round light pool sits on the stripes and the right-hand figure while everything else dims and blurs; the pool core runs hot (8% clipped).

ae.note: A yellow ring pings around the right-hand region while everything outside a feathered circle there darkens to about 60% black by 1.0 s, so the region is clearly spotlit; vs Premiere: AE dims without blurring and marks the region with a thin ring instead of Premiere's warm light pool and soft surround.

cards.name: Route / connector line draw
cards.summary: A glowing line draws itself from one point to another (city to city, cause to effect). Premiere draws a thin white-core line with the plug-in's blue-violet glow and no end dot; After Effects lands an amber dot at the end.
use_for: trade, migration, travel or supply routes on a map
linking two people or places in an explainer
data-viz connector between two chart elements
avoid: curved routes: both effects draw straight lines (use a shape layer with the 'Write On Arrow' preset for curves)
Premiere: the line is the Lightning effect straightened (Amplitude 0); its glow colour is the plug-in default blue and cannot be set, check a frame
more than two or three lines at once
cards.keyframes_note: Draw-on in 0.8 s. After Effects Beam: with Length 1 the beam spans tail = Time*2-1 to head = Time*2 of the path (measured on the gallery render: Length 0.7 / Time 0.5 covered 15%-85%), so Time 0 -> 0.5 grows it from start to end and holding 0.5 keeps the full line; Time past 0.5 makes it leave. Premiere grows the line by keyframing End point from the start point to the destination. Keep the start/end points identical between apps ([0.27, 0.57] = [518, 616], [0.72, 0.35] = [1382, 378] in 1920x1080).

verified.note: A thin straight white-violet line grows from the left of frame toward the right (partial at 0.2 s, full at 1.0 s) with no end dot.
verified.recheck: 2026-10-13: re-rendered in live wave 1 (frames the old verdict was judged on: pve/work/gallery_pre_fix/)

previous.why: the verify step rewrote the summary from this render (its rule for 'wrong'); the rewritten card has not been rendered again
re-rendered with the corrected text and values (live wave 1); the new frame matches the corrected card

ae.note: A thin amber-edged line grows from the left foreground block toward the upper right (short at 0.2 s, full length at 1.0 s) and lands an amber dot at its end; vs Premiere: same path and timing as Premiere's line, but amber instead of blue-violet and with the end dot.

cards.name: Chart / shape pulse glow
cards.summary: A graphic element with transparency (map state, chart bar, icon, key number) pulses with a coloured glow to pull the eye; in Premiere the Edge Glow is only a faint tint on the brightest pixels (render-checked on footage, not yet on an alpha graphic), so the pulse is subtle, while the After Effects version glows from the alpha edge.
use_for: highlighting one state or bar in an animated map or chart
icon or logo emphasis in an explainer
avoid: full-frame footage: use it on a graphic clip / layer with alpha
pulsing several elements at once
low-contrast glow colour against the background
cards.keyframes_note: Two pulses over 1.4 s; repeat the pairs to hold longer. Apply to the graphic clip/layer itself, not the footage under it. After Effects glows from the alpha edge (Glow Based On 1 = Alpha Channel) with A & B colours; Premiere's Edge Glow blooms the graphic's bright pixels and Colorize 100 tints it. ('Alpha Glow' in Premiere is the true alpha-edge glow but was not render-tested.) Premiere's bloom stays a faint tint: at Width/Height 15 with Size 40 the gallery render showed no readable glow, and the re-render at Size 60 with Width/Height 200 was still only a faint tint on footage; for a strong pulse use After Effects or test 'Alpha Glow'.

verified.note: No visible change from the first render: at the 1.0 s peak only a faint yellow-green tint sits on a small round motif, lamps and plants (mean diff about 4/255, frame luma pulse +6 at 0.3 s and +4 at 1.0 s), so Size 60 with Width/Height 200 still gives no readable glow on footage, and no in-range value clearly fixes it (the card's Size 100 demo is just as faint), so the summary was rewritten.

ae.note: On a full-frame opaque layer the alpha-based Glow floods the entire frame orange-yellow at both samples (mean luma about 196 against 106 clean), so the alpha-edge pulse needs a graphic with transparency to be judged; vs Premiere: Premiere's version is only a faint tint on footage; neither half has been tried on an alpha graphic.

cards.name: Title disintegrates to dust
cards.summary: A title breaks into fine grains that warp and blow sideways until nothing is left, like text turning to dust.
use_for: ending a title or name card dramatically
avoid: full-frame footage (it dissolves to black): use it on a title / graphic with alpha
long durations: over ~1.5 s it reads as a render fault
small body text
cards.keyframes_note: Out move over the title's last 1.0 s (negative times = from the layer's end). The end keys sit at -0.04 (the last frame), never 0: a key time of 0 means the clip START, so [0, peak] plays the move at the head (the gallery render showed exactly that). Order matters: warp and smear first, then Block Dissolve (2 px blocks) eats the result away so the grains thin out to nothing. Premiere's new Directional Blur uses Angle 90 for horizontal; After Effects' Directional Blur (match 'ADBE Motion Blur') uses Direction 90.

verified.note: With the end keys at -0.04 the 0.2 s and 1.0 s frames are now intact and the out move plays at the tail as intended: from about 1.0 s the picture warps, smears sideways and breaks into fine grains that thin to near black by the last frame (103c, taken at 1.6 s; on full-frame footage it ends black, as the avoid list says).

ae.note: From the first frame the constant Right/Left Twist bends the whole picture into a skewed shape with black wedges in the corners, long before the out move, which only starts adding grain and darkening at 1.0 s; vs Premiere: Premiere's 0.2 s and 1.0 s frames are intact because all its distortion is keyed to the tail.

previous.why: after_effects changed: Right Twist and Left Twist were constants and twist the layer even at Scatter 0; keying them from 0 alongside the Scatter ramp keeps the picture intact until the last 1.0 s.; not rendered again
